pr_title: sql: add option to use lookup join for db-scope virtual tables
pr_body:
information_schema and pg_catalog are always scoped to a database. Before this change, we would always look up all descriptors to materialize virtual tables, even if we only care about descriptors in the current database. The new approach: scan the namespace table to find the relevant descriptors and then only resolve those.

On my local machine where I loaded up a few megabytes of descriptors into 6k databases, a simple query like `SELECT * FROM information_schema.sequences` takes 1.2s without the setting enabled and 1ms with it.

Fixes #90115

Epic: CRDB-20865
    
Release note (performance improvement): Tables in `pg_catalog` and
`information_schema` (when not explicitly referenced as
`"".information_schema`) may now be much faster if the current database has
a small number of relations relative to the total number in the cluster.

Okay, so the problematic lines are here:
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/accea9d27aeb5afe4d05b23323b8d4b1fac04c77/pkg/sql/virtual_schema.go#L253-L263

@AlexTalks maybe you recall the motivation for these limitations?

Well, for one, I think I messed up what `partial` meant. So that solves that. 

I think there remains two issues:
1) Is it safe to call `GetAllDescriptors` inside a generator callback? I don't think it is because it'll lead to concurrent access to catalog data structures. I'm going to investigate that separately. 

2) For the returning of many rows, maybe yes, maybe no. Consider specifically the case here. I want to only get all the descriptors for the database and not all the descriptors in the system. I don't really buy the memory argument in this case because the descriptors are at least on the same order as all the rows we're going to get and they are now all memory monitored. 

I think my conclusion is
1) I think the key takeaway here is that I'm using `partial` incorrectly. 
2) The use of populate here instead of generate is probably safer and probably not worse. 

Do those conclusion make sense to you?

Alright I added a pair of commits to rename `partial` to `incomplete` and to put in an assertion that `incomplete` indexes not be combined with `generator`. Do you see a problem with the use of `populate` here?

> Is it safe to call GetAllDescriptors inside a generator callback?

In theory, IIRC, the generator callback has been carefully designed to have 0 true concurrency. If this doesn't actually work, I agree we would have issues. The goal of the whole generator business is to make it easier to write these really stateful iterators using the Go stack rather than having to hand-assemble a giant confusing stateful mess for every table. But, it's key to your point that they don't actually have concurrency or else lots of things would break.

So if we investigate something it would be making sure that the generator callback isn't actually executing concurrently with anything.

> For the returning of many rows, maybe yes, maybe no.

I think in this particular case using populate sounds fine. The flexibility is there for cases that might need to return many more rows without memory monitoring. I guess we should add some more clarity to the doc strings about when to use which.

issue_context.title: sql: DB-scope virtual tables are slow despite a small DB
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

CockroachDB offers per-database metadata schemas `information_schema` and `pg_catalog`. The tables in these schemas are implemented "virtually"; instead of being real tables, we run some code over the internal metadata structures to generate the output. Today, in order to populate the correct set of descriptors, we unconditionally fetch all descriptors. In cases where individual databases are not large, but the total number of descriptors is large, virtual tables are shockingly slow. Importantly, these virtual tables don't need to look at most of these descriptors.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We can avoid looking at the unwanted descriptors by performing a lookup first against the namespace table and then fetching the descriptors in the database.

**Additional context**
This approach won't help with cases like https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/83626 where individual schemas or databases have large numbers of objects. 

Epic: CRDB-20865

Jira issue: CRDB-20592
